english.title: Induce or procure person to vote at parliamentary or local elections when subject to legal incapacity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of an illegal practice in that you knowingly induced or procured **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to

(A)_[vote in person as an elector]_
(B)_[vote in person as proxy]_
(C)_[vote by post as an elector]_
(D)_[vote by post as proxy]_
(E)_[apply to vote by proxy]_
(F)_[apply to vote by post as elector]_

at

(G)_[a parliamentary election,]_
(H)_[parliamentary elections,]_
(I)_[a local government election,]_
(J)_[local government elections,]_

namely, **(..SPECIFY ELECTION OR ELECTIONS..), knowing that

(K)_[he]_
(L)_[she]_

(M)_[that election,]_
(N)_[elections of that kind,]_

english.legislation: Contrary to sections 61(1)(a), (5) and (7) and 169 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowingly induce or procure a person to
vote in person or by post as an elector or proxy or apply to vote by proxy or as elector
at a parliamentary or local government election or elections
knowing that he or she was subject to a legal incapacity to vote at that election or elections of that kind

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
61(7) An offence under this section shall be an illegal practice but -
(a) the court before whom a person is convicted of any such offence may, if they think it just in the special circumstances of the case, mitigate or entirely remit any incapacity imposed by virtue of section 173; and (b) a candidate shall not be liable, nor shall his election be avoided, for an illegal practice under this section of any agent of his other than an offence under subsection (5) above.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 176

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
